subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this broad WhatsApp cron incident be resolved by landing the schedule-activation replay fix and tracking emergency stop/delete separately, or should one combined change define cron removal and gateway stop as an emergency outbound halt?
rationale: The replay bug has a concrete candidate PR, but the remaining stop/delete behavior changes user-visible operator semantics across cron, task cancellation, gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery.

options.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
options.body: Review or replace the open schedule-activation PR, then track a separate product-scoped emergency stop/delete design for active outbound sends.

options.title: Require One Combined Fix
options.body: Keep this issue open until one implementation covers restart replay, active cron cancellation on remove, and a user-facing emergency outbound halt.

options.title: Narrow To Replay Only
options.body: Declare stop/delete emergency controls out of scope here and close only after the replay fix lands.

recommendation.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
recommendation.body: Review or replace the open schedule-activation PR, then track a separate product-scoped emergency stop/delete design for active outbound sends.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron service ownership/status work touched the same persisted cron update surface, and the remaining choice is a product boundary across core runtime behavior.
